items.model_correction: A relayed proposal's source_edge_id is NOT rewritten at each hop, so the emitter is generally neither the source node nor the unit that opened that edge. Attribution is now checked as the path property: the emitter must stand on the adopted return path walked from the source.

items.title: Edge-scoped liability continuation (compare >=7 designs)
findings: The defect is real but not where the tests look. Every LC-2 fixture is density 1.0 or the synthetic _pair(); at density 1.0 all 6 edges are answered and 0 are stranded. At n_auth=3 density=0.6 seed=5, 13 of 39 edges are stranded, 5 parents wait forever, 10 nodes hold children_outstanding.

Five of the seven metric counters are declared and never incremented. CLOSED_CHILD_EDGES reads 0 while 6 edges reached terminal_status=terminal, so the denominator guard fires because the counter is dead. Three further assertions in that test are vacuously satisfied.

terminal_status is written in exactly one place (_record_outcome, v5.py:1421), reached only for outcome-channel terminals. 0 edges are terminal without child evidence on any fixture. So incrementing the closure counters together at that one site would make WITH_ACCEPTED == closed and WITHOUT_EVIDENCE == 0 assertions about one increment agreeing with itself. The metric must be DERIVED from edge state.

The coalescing test's premise is inverted: e/sep/coal/2 (coalesced) is answered correctly and immediately by the receiving endpoint; e/sep/coal/1 (ADOPTED) has no lifecycle record because the node is still OPEN with reason candidate_silent. The test reads both edges when only one can yet have an answer.
items.what_lc2_must_be: A continuation for the ADOPTED edge, not the coalesced one. It must not close an edge on the opener's assertion; its metric must be derived rather than a family of counters incremented together; and it must distinguish legitimately-still-open from permanently-stranded, which no current fixture can do because none drives a search to a conclusion.
